answer: To counter Sybil attacks, an agent network can require continuous Verifiable Delay Functions, forcing nodes to periodically broadcast sequential state proofs. Operating like a sieve protecting a liquidity oasis, this forces an adversary across a meadow of fake identities to dedicate scarce single-threaded CPU cycles cracking each mathematical walnut in real time. However, this continuous computation wastes energy and handicaps honest agents operating on low-power embedded processors.
